Bacterial Red disease.description: A bacterial infection caused by Aeromonas or Pseudomonas species, resulting in red lesions and hemorrhaging on the skin.
symptoms: Red patches or lesions on skin
Bacterial Red disease.treatment: Isolate affected fish immediately. Use antibiotics such as oxytetracycline or amoxicillin in the water. Perform 30% water change daily. Maintain water temperature between 24-26°C.
Bacterial Red disease.prevention: Maintain good water quality, avoid overcrowding, quarantine new fish for 2 weeks before introducing to the tank.
Bacterial Red disease.urgency: Treat within 24-48 hours to prevent spread.

Bacterial diseases - Aeromoniasis.description: Infection caused by Aeromonas hydrophila bacteria, commonly known as 'Motile Aeromonas Septicemia' or MAS.
Bacterial diseases - Aeromoniasis.treatment: Administer antibiotics (enrofloxacin or florfenicol) as directed by a vet. Add aquarium salt (1 tsp per gallon). Improve water filtration and perform frequent water changes.
Bacterial diseases - Aeromoniasis.prevention: Reduce stress factors, maintain optimal water parameters (pH 7.0-7.5, ammonia 0 ppm), avoid physical injuries to fish.
Bacterial diseases - Aeromoniasis.urgency: Immediate treatment required — can be fatal within days.

Bacterial gill disease.description: Bacterial infection affecting the gills, caused by Flavobacterium branchiophilum, leading to respiratory distress.
Bacterial gill disease.treatment: Use potassium permanganate bath (2 mg/L for 1 hour). Apply chloramine-T treatment. Increase aeration in the tank. Consult a vet for antibiotic prescription if severe.
Bacterial gill disease.prevention: Ensure adequate oxygen levels, avoid overcrowding, maintain clean filters, and perform regular water testing.
Bacterial gill disease.urgency: Treat within 48 hours to prevent mass mortality.

Fungal diseases Saprolegniasis.description: Fungal infection caused by Saprolegnia species, appearing as white or gray cotton-like growth on the fish body.
symptoms: White or gray fluffy patches on skin
Cotton-like growth around eyes or mouth
Fungal diseases Saprolegniasis.treatment: Use antifungal treatment such as malachite green (0.1 mg/L) or salt baths (3 g/L for 10 minutes). Remove infected fish to a quarantine tank. Improve water temperature to 24°C.
Fungal diseases Saprolegniasis.prevention: Maintain water temperature above 18°C, treat any wounds or injuries promptly, avoid sharp objects in the tank.
Fungal diseases Saprolegniasis.urgency: Begin treatment within 72 hours to prevent secondary infections.

Healthy Fish.description: The fish appears healthy with no signs of disease.
Healthy Fish.treatment: No treatment required. Continue regular maintenance.
Healthy Fish.prevention: Maintain regular feeding schedule, perform weekly 20% water changes, monitor water parameters (pH, ammonia, nitrite, temperature) weekly.
Healthy Fish.urgency: No action required. Schedule routine checkup in 30 days.

Parasitic diseases.description: Infections caused by external parasites such as Ichthyophthirius (Ich/White Spot), Dactylogyrus (flukes), or Argulus (fish lice).
symptoms: White spots on skin or fins (Ich)
Parasitic diseases.treatment: Raise water temperature to 30°C to speed up parasite life cycle. Use formalin or copper-based treatments as directed. For Ich: treat with malachite green + formalin combo for 7-10 days.
Parasitic diseases.prevention: Quarantine all new fish for 2 weeks, sterilize equipment, avoid introducing wild-caught fish without inspection.
Parasitic diseases.urgency: Treat promptly — parasites spread rapidly to all tank inhabitants.

Viral diseases White tail disease.description: Caused by Macrobrachium rosenbergii nodavirus (MrNV), primarily affecting freshwater prawns and some fish, causing white discoloration of the tail.
symptoms: White discoloration of tail and hind body
Viral diseases White tail disease.treatment: No specific antiviral treatment available. Isolate and remove severely affected fish. Improve water quality and reduce stress. Boost immunity with vitamin C-enriched feed.
Viral diseases White tail disease.prevention: Source fish/prawns from certified disease-free hatcheries. Disinfect water with UV sterilizer. Avoid mixing species from different sources.
Viral diseases White tail disease.urgency: Isolate immediately — viral diseases can wipe out entire stock.
